title: _poll_for_state race: deadline check ordered BEFORE fold_plan_state, so a successfully-folded plan state from a blocking dispatch is missed when subprocess wall-clock exceeds the timeout budget
raised_by: ARIA-V10.5 F-024 production validation endurance (v10-5-f-024-validation-20260521-155112) — 3 cycles completed, 0 reached evaluate_plan, all 3 terminated with different early-termination verdicts (primary_revision_failed, cross_review_unavailable, challenger_unavailable) all tracing to the same race in _poll_for_state
resolved_by: ARIA-V10.5 Phase 5 (Tier-1 _poll_for_state loop reorder: observe state before checking deadline)

smoking_gun_timeline.17:47:25: drainer entered _run_challenge_and_cross_review_phase for round 2; agent_claim_created for round-2 challenger (AIR-aria-challenger-planner-e2306805); deadline = 17:47:25 + 600s = 17:57:25

post_termination_verification.method: PYTHONPATH=aria-kernel:. python3 -c 'from aria_kernel.plan_convergence import fold_plan_state; print(fold_plan_state(plan_id="plan-cyc-20260521T172723Z-auto", base_dir="./aria-tools"))'
post_termination_verification.interpretation: The kernel state machine was in the EXACT target state the drainer was polling for. The state was just missed by 31s due to the race.

structural_root_cause.loop_order_bug: _poll_for_state's while loop checks `time.monotonic() < deadline` at the TOP of the loop, then calls fold_plan_state, then dispatch_one_pending_planner_request (which blocks synchronously for the entire subprocess wall-clock). When dispatch returns after a long subprocess, the loop iterates back to the while condition — which fails because deadline expired during the dispatch — and the function returns None. The state THAT WAS JUST FOLDED INSIDE THE DISPATCH never gets observed because fold_plan_state runs AFTER the deadline check, not before.
structural_root_cause.why_dispatch_is_synchronous: The V10.4 Phase 3.H docstring on convergence_drainer.py:308 documents this explicitly: 'blocks on real Claude subprocess (~90-180s) when there is one'. The architectural decision was for the drainer to OWN dispatch (inline rather than delegate to the external planner daemon, closes F-016). But the inline dispatch's synchronous wall-clock now coexists with the deadline check ordering bug — the consequence was structurally invisible until F-024 unblocked deeper into the round flow.
structural_root_cause.lesson: When a poll loop's dispatch action IS the state-changer, the state check MUST run before the deadline check. Otherwise long-running successful dispatches are indistinguishable from infinite hangs. The poll loop's invariant is: state observation has temporal priority over budget enforcement, because budget enforcement only matters if NO state change happened.
structural_root_cause.tier_1_anchor: Same root-cause family as F-024 (SSoT drift between drainer and kernel) but at the temporal-ordering layer instead of the parameter-passing layer. F-024 closed the drainer↔kernel max_rounds parameter parity; F-025 closes the drainer's own poll loop temporal ordering.

tier_1_architectural_fix.scope: Reorder _poll_for_state's loop body so fold_plan_state runs BEFORE the deadline check, with state-match as a strictly higher priority terminal condition than deadline expiry.

before_after.before: while time.monotonic() < deadline: { check_stop(); state=fold(); if match: return state; dispatch(); sleep(); }
before_after.after: while True: { check_stop(); state=fold(); if match: return state; if time.monotonic() >= deadline: return None; dispatch(); sleep(); }

tier_1_architectural_fix.why_this_terminates: The loop still terminates on (a) ARIA_STOP, (b) state-match (happy path), (c) deadline-expiry-AND-state-not-match (sad path). The only behavior change is that a state-match observed AT THE SAME ITERATION as deadline expiry now wins — which is the correct architectural priority because the state was provably produced before the deadline (since it's observable at the iteration's top).
tier_1_architectural_fix.why_this_is_tier_1: The fix doesn't tune a parameter; it changes the structural invariant of the loop so the race CANNOT occur regardless of subprocess wall-clock. A 25-minute subprocess that successfully folds at t=24:59 is now observed; only a subprocess that never folds (true hang) hits the deadline path.
files_changed: aria-kernel/tests/invariants/v10/test_phase_v10_5_phase_5_poll_state_race.py (4 Tier-3 invariants — source-level ordering, dispatch-folds-state observed, deadline-vs-state priority, ARIA_STOP precedence preserved)

expected_impact_on_endurance.before_fix: Any cycle whose dispatch wall-clock for ANY envelope (primary revision, challenger, cross_review) exceeds challenger_timeout_seconds terminates with the corresponding *_unavailable / *_failed verdict, regardless of whether the bridge ACTUALLY folded the state. F-024 (kernel terminal-state derivation) cannot be exercised because no cycle reaches evaluate_plan.
expected_impact_on_endurance.after_fix: A dispatch that successfully folds plan state inside its wall-clock — even if that wall-clock exceeded challenger_timeout_seconds — is observed by the next iteration's top-of-loop fold_plan_state. Only TRULY hung subprocesses (or subprocesses that fail to fold) hit the deadline. F-024's evaluate_plan path is now reachable: cycles can complete all 3 P+C+CR rounds, reach round 3 evaluate_plan, kernel emits plan_evaluated event with terminal_state, verdict_provenance fires.
